propositions: Two concurrent reducer cache writers use the same fixed .cache.json.tmp temp file, allowing one to rename it into place while another continues mutating the now-visible final file.
A cache publication can carry the current hash with stale state fields when concurrent reductions observe different event generations and splice their results.
write_cache in _cache.py and corrupt-CREATE handling in _processors.py both publish cache independently with fixed-temp artifacts instead of a shared atomic mechanism.
A cache-bypassing replay oracle should always match a current-hash cache hit, but concurrent non-serialized writes violate this invariant.

The repair consolidates all cache publication through canonical atomic_write with unique private temps, routes corrupt-CREATE through write_cache, and extends gitignore to exclude private temp artifacts.
